validation_notes: Processed 14 unique people from 15 RUAL CSV rows. Checked 2 local RUAL documents before internet research: annual report and consolidated financial statements. Completed 14 round_1 person research notes plus one overview note. CEO/General Director for 2024 is Evgeny Viktorovich Nikitin. Local annual report confirms 2024 board composition and shows that Anton Egorov was not a 2024 board member; his CSV role date is post-2024 and later sources show 2025 appointment. Education not confirmed for Victor Mann and Karen Li; Alexander Popov education is based on MarketScreener rather than primary RUSAL bio. Weak sources used: MarketScreener for Alexander Popov education/career and some board-member cross-checks; SimplyWallSt/search-indexed HKEX snippets for Anton Egorov education because his role is post-2024. No unresolved namesake mixing: basketball player Anton Egorov and literary Evgeny Shvarts results were rejected. No h-index values were added because none were verified. Search considered complete because all local RUAL PDFs were checked first, official RUSAL/HKEX disclosures and securities prospectus were used where available, and repeated education/career/research/namesake searches did not reveal stronger public biographies for the sparse cases. QUALITY PASS ROUND 1 (2026-07-31): Step 0 baseline check against git HEAD (commit f973022) found no regression for RUAL -- all notes, professional_experience/education descriptions and source citations on disk were already at or above the committed baseline; no restoration needed. Simple-omission desyncs fixed (16 qualification_degree fills, all traceable to explicit qualification wording already cited in existing sources): Nikitin education (Specialist degree, MBA), Popov CPA (Professional certification), Chan education (Bachelor's degree) and membership (Professional certification), Zonneveld education (Master's degree), Parker education (Bachelor's degree), Burnham education x2 (Bachelor's degree, Master's degree), Shvarts education (Specialist degree) and both degrees (Doctoral degree, for Kandidat and Doktor Nauk, the closest enum fit for Russian post-graduate scientific degrees), Egorov MBA education entry (MBA), Vasilenko education (Specialist degree, based on the explicit 'экономист-бухгалтер' qualification, not the Bologna-era 'master's degree' implied by the program label), Galenskaya education (Specialist degree), Mironov education and degree (Master's degree). Left null on purpose (insufficient explicit qualification wording in the cited source, not a simple omission): Popov's two MarketScreener 'undergraduate/graduate degree' entries, Egorov's MSU physics-and-law and RAS graduate-studies-diploma entries (weak secondary snippet sources only), Albrecht's Bauman MSTU entry (no explicit qualification title or year in the cited annual-report fact, unlike the other Soviet/Russian-era cases that had one). Genuine inconsistencies investigated and documented in person-level notes (values kept were already the round_1 resolution; this round added the explicit rejected-alternative reasoning that was missing from the JSON notes field): Shvarts RUSAL appointment date (annual report/prospectus '20 April 2020' kept over Vedomosti's 'since March 2020', treated as company-filing vs. secondary-paraphrase, not a real conflict); Mann technical-director start year (Light Metal Age 'since 2005' kept over MarketScreener's bare '2004-12-31', for the same reason). GICS corrections: Albrecht's professional_experience[0] (organization = RUSAL/RUSAL Management/UC RUSAL SUPPORT DMCC, all RUSAL Group entities) was mislabeled Industrials/Transportation/Marine Transportation (New Name) and corrected to Materials/Materials/Metals & Mining, matching the top-level company classification and the real business of every named entity in that entry. Six heterogeneous multi-employer aggregate entries that had been assigned a single wrong commercial GICS label were nulled (sector/industry_group/industry set back to null) rather than left mislabeled, because no single gics_taxonomy.json row is truthfully correct for a mixed list of employers in genuinely different industries -- this matches the precedent already set in research_notes/RUAL/gics_quality_round_20260728.md for two other RUAL aggregate entries: Zonneveld's 'Capitalmind, ING Bank, Vimetco and trade councils' (was Financials/Banks/Banks -- wrong because Vimetco is an aluminium producer, Materials, not a bank); Parker's 'SICM, Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, EF Hutton, Chateau Maris, The Westaim Corporation' (was Financials/Banks/Banks -- wrong because Chateau Maris is a wine estate, Consumer Staples, not a financial firm); Burnham's 'Cambridge Global Capital/Advisors, Deutsche Asset Management, UN, US State Department...' (was Financials/Financial Services/Capital Markets -- wrong because the UN and US State Department are government/international bodies that should never carry a commercial GICS label); Mironov's 'Chelpipe Group, Rimera Group, Credit Suisse, Renaissance Capital' (was Financials/Financial Services/Consumer Finance -- Consumer Finance describes none of the four employers, directly analogous to the insurer-vs-Consumer-Finance example); Egorov's 'Russian Post and prior legal/management roles' (was Industrials/Commercial & Professional Services/Professional Services -- wrong as a whole-entry label because Russian Post is a postal/logistics operator, Sidanko was an oil company and MDM Bank is a bank, only Ernst & Young CIS genuinely fits Professional Services); Albrecht's professional_experience[1] 'En+ Holding, ALPG, VimpelCom, Rostelecom, STS Media, NTV Plus...' (was Communication Services/Telecommunication Services/Diversified Telecommunication Services -- wrong because it mixes real telecom operators with a metals/energy holding company and broadcast/media companies). No other non-null GICS entries in this file needed correction; entries already null for other people's direct RUSAL employer rows were left untouched as an existing, consistent, deliberate pattern across the whole file (RUSAL, the covered company itself, is not separately GICS-tagged per person), and Shvarts's RAS/HSE/WWF/BCC aggregate and Vasilenko's/Galenskaya's/Popov's other aggregates were left null as already-correct per the 2026-07-28 precedent. Bounded gap follow-up (one attempt each, per task scope) for the three fields flagged in round_1 as 'insufficient reliable source': Victor Mann education, Karen Li education/biography, and Evgeny Shvarts h-index. Fresh, non-overlapping queries were selected for each (documented in research_notes/RUAL/quality_pass_round1_20260731.md and in each person's notes field) but could not be executed because this session's WebSearch tool reported its call budget exhausted (200/200) on every attempt; no new search results were obtained, so all three fields remain null/undetermined, explicitly logged as still-unresolved rather than re-confirmed as absent, so a future pass does not silently repeat this same failed attempt without knowing it never actually ran.
